- scripts/ci_budget_watch.py:139 (main function) | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The script prints `::warning::` when it encounters errors, but the `try...except` blocks that catch API errors also swallow the error and return 0. While this is "fail-open", it might be useful to ensure that the job doesn't mistakenly signal success to GitHub Actions if the logic itself is fundamentally broken.
  WHY: The script always exits with 0 even if it fails to list existing issues or label existence, meaning the job could fail to report budget issues silently.
- scripts/ci_budget_watch.py:181-196 (Main loop and issue creation) | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: As noted in previous rounds, the script lists issues and then creates new ones without a proper lock. While the impact is limited to a duplicate issue, if multiple `main` branch pushes happen close together (e.g., within the job's runtime window), the `existing` snapshot might become stale, leading to redundant issue creation.
  WHY: The `existing` variable is populated once at the beginning of `main()`. If concurrent `ci_budget_watch.py` processes run (e.g., due to rapid pushes), they all use the same label marker check and will all try to create an issue if the label marker is missing from the initial `existing` set.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The new invocation detector pins one exact variable spelling (`"${AUTOFIX_FAILURE_HEAL_PY}"`) and one layout where the executable and subcommand sit on the same line. A future call site that uses a renamed helper variable (e.g. `"${DIFFERENT_VAR}"`) and places the subcommand on a continuation line so the `\\\n` no longer follows the executable/subcommand fragment would not match either the `invocations` check (different variable) or the `calls` check (different `\\\n` placement), so `len(invocations) == len(calls)` would still pass for the 4 known sites even after a 5th call site had been added.
  WHY: A future `autofix-failure-fingerprint` call that omits `--support-sha` would slip past the new guard. Its failure marker would land without a support SHA, and support-aware fingerprint processing in `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py` would ignore or mis-classify the marker, breaking the cap and stale-head pinning that `#6625`/`#6938` introduced.

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The invocation detector pins one exact variable spelling (`"${AUTOFIX_FAILURE_HEAL_PY}"`). A future single-line invocation that uses a different spelling (e.g. `"$AUTOFIX_FAILURE_HEAL_PY"` without braces, or a renamed helper variable) would not appear in `invocations`, so `len(invocations) != len(calls)` and the assertion fails — but the failure message would not identify which invocation was missed, and the per-block `--support-sha` check only runs on `calls` (multi-line calls), so a single-line call that matches the count but omits `--support-sha` would pass unchecked.
  WHY: The test's structural pin is weaker than intended. A future single-line invocation without `--support-sha` could pass if it uses the expected variable spelling, because the test only checks `--support-sha` in multi-line call blocks.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py:3640-3643 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The new single-line-call detector (added by the last run) matches only one exact spelling, `"${AUTOFIX_FAILURE_HEAL_PY}" autofix-failure-fingerprint`, and only when the executable and subcommand sit on the same line. Two future layouts evade both checks: (a) a single-line call through a different spelling, e.g. `python3 "$AUTOFIX_FAILURE_HEAL_PY" autofix-failure-fingerprint ...`; (b) a wrapped call where the executable and subcommand are split across lines, e.g. `python3 "${AUTOFIX_FAILURE_HEAL_PY}" \` followed by `autofix-failure-fingerprint --head-sha ...` (subcommand first, no trailing backslash on the exec line) — the split at line 3638 on `"autofix-failure-fingerprint \\\n"` also misses (b), since the subcommand line does not end with a backslash. In either layout, the equality assertion at line 3643 still sees 4 == 4 and the per-block check at 3644-3647 never reaches the new call, so an invocation that omits `--support-sha "${REVIEW_SUPPORT_SHA:-}"` passes the guard. Its failure marker is then emitted without the verified support SHA, and support-version-aware cap/stale-marker consumers ignore it (the exact regression class #6625/#6938 closed). Verified against the current ref: the workflow's 4 real call sites (review_autofix.yml:4869, 6206, 6297, 6575) all use the pinned spelling, so the test passes today; the gap is only for future call sites.
  WHY: CI guard (static-checks) reports pass while a new fingerprint call site omits the support SHA; the defect surfaces later as `NOOP_RECOVERY_FINGERPRINT_CAP_STALE_SUPPORT`-style ignores instead of a red CI step, i.e. the structural pin this test was rewritten to provide silently does not cover all invocation shapes.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
